Before you buy

Check the power station's maximum solar input. If it accepts only 200W, connecting 400W of panels generally won't make it charge faster than that input limit allows.

Check the voltage range and connector compatibility. The 400W panel above has a listed open-circuit voltage of 45.3V, which is too high for some smaller stations.

Consider the season. A 200–300W setup can work well in summer, but winter recharging may require 400–700W or more, depending on your location and sunlight. Source: Held in Reserve

My recommendation: Start with 200W for budget-friendly everyday use, or 300–400W if you want faster recharging.
